scope: Real TCP EOF in a progressed scenario, native map/world logout and save, retired session destruction, fresh-session login and actual empty-instance destruction
finding: No additional production defect was observed. All32 native disconnect/fresh-session cases pass: existing instances retain native position/stage/progress, while actual DestroyInstance loss restarts at the recorded entrance with stage0 and empty progress. This commit adds regression coverage and audit evidence; server implementation and runtime binaries are unchanged.
implementation: Extend the existing native Scenario fixture at stage1 with actual criteria1 and7/33. Move the scratch Player eight yards with native PlayerRelocation so the current position differs from its recorded entrance.

Close the real loopback TCP peer on either the realm or instance channel. Execute actual Map::UpdateSessions and World::UpdateSessions; require native forced teardown, Player deletion, map/world session removal, both closed/detached sockets and a persisted offline checkpoint. Do not call LogoutPlayer or SetMap to manufacture the disconnect outcome.

Destroy the retired WorldSession after native teardown and release its fixture owner. Construct a new WorldSession with new realm/instance loopback transports, require initial login serial0 and clean loading/map/teardown state, then execute the accepted login opcode, native instance-link dispatch, full SQL holder and delayed map admission.

For the second disconnect, destroy only the empty fixture-owned map1460 instance through native MapInstanced::DestroyInstance. Assert both map and Scenario are absent before reconnecting. Keep the real saved checkpoint unchanged, including its current boot marker; this is actual instance loss rather than the prior old-boot simulation.

Decode actual queued initialization and scenario packets. A live instance must retain stage1, ActiveSteps, criteria progress and later position; a destroyed instance must create stage0 at its entrance without old criteria. Preserve health321, sickness598000ms, item25 durability27, mover/corpse state and duplicate-notification protection.

native_cases.contexts: Four parent raid-difficulty contexts and two travel directions repeat both Broken Shore factions. Direction0 uses realm EOF/early loading finish; direction1 uses instance EOF/late loading finish, with both live/destroyed outcomes. Loading order and channel are deliberately paired here; all cross-combinations are not claimed.
native_cases.retained_regressions: The previous64 same-session live/old-boot relogs and48 scenario initialization/fresh teleport cases remain in the same native execution.

native_data.routing: Use the existing runtime DB2/world stores and the committed shared faction route resolver. No invented Scenario, LFG record, stage or criteria state is injected.

method_and_limits: EOF is observed by an actual asynchronous socket read; the test advances the native map/world session cycles and uses their logout/save path. It then explicitly destroys the fully retired session. A new post-authentication WorldSession, realm/instance sockets and login request are created; no stale Player/session is reused.

Socket association and login start at the established post-authentication fixture boundary. TLS/authentication/HMAC/encryption exchange, account queue admission and encrypted client delivery are not exercised. Schema-only scratch account0/characters are used, not personal account data.

Map workers belong only to the disposable native fixture and are stopped for deterministic execution. Explicit native DestroyInstance exercises map/Scenario deletion and subsequent real factory reconstruction, not expiration of the production unload timer or arbitrary cross-thread interleavings.

PlayerRelocation provides distinct later/entrance positions for persistence checks; it does not establish client movement/collision. Criteria are awarded through native type92 events, not by writing Scenario internals.

No WoW client was operated. Scenario UI, actor/quest traversal and completion, visuals/voice, camera, pet portrait and reconnect under actual network latency remain client checks. No actor-state serialization or exact-stage recovery after a server crash is claimed.

World access is read-only; character/auth writes and session destruction affect only disposable schema-only test data. Runtime configuration, binaries, certificates, DLLs, logs and extracted data are preserved.
checks: Test-TrialHelyaControlNative.ps1 -VerifyReleaseBinary passed32 real TCP EOF/fresh-session cases,16 per faction,16 live and16 actually destroyed instances. Each scenario/instance-loss/channel combination occurs four times. Existing64 relogs,48 scenario cases and288 incremental/full timestamp assertions also pass.

Native EOF map/world updates delete the Player, remove map/world session registrations, close/reset both socket slots and detach socket ownership. Native save retains the real versioned current-boot checkpoint and offline character state. The old session is destroyed and a clean new constructor/login/socket/SQL path reconstructs the Player. No direct logout or fabricated map removal is used for the disconnect outcome.

Canonical exception-bounded Map::UpdateSessions and World::UpdateSessions retain calls to WorldSession::Update and LogoutPlayer. Canonical MapInstanced::DestroyInstance calls ScenarioMgr::RemoveScenario. Existing Release checks also preserve shared faction routing, actual caller admission and absolute scenario progress timestamps. Native input hashes bind current fixtures/source to the original final-link game.lib and deployed executable.

Existing280 loading-order,392 map-loading,392 early-loading,392 linked-cancellation,392 instance-link,392 deferred-query,280 session,168 aggregate-login and two socket-owner probes pass, alongside configured spirit/ghost/graveyard/Helya regressions. Native DBErrors is empty and Server.log has no ERROR. Schema-only scratch character/auth databases (167 tables) and SQL user were removed.

Canonical worldserver.exe, MAP and final-link game.lib match the83758f7d audited Release. No implementation change, rebuild, migration or runtime deployment was needed. No worldserver/bnetserver was started or stopped in this task and none remains; runtime configuration/data/certificates/DLLs/logs were preserved. Client checks remain pending as listed in method_and_limits.
